newsitem.title: UK: British Energy sees prices slowing in H2.
newsitem.headline: British Energy sees prices slowing in H2.

text.p: Nuclear electricity generator British Energy said it did not expect the trend of higher prices in the market seen in the first half to continue in the second half. In a statement with half-year results, its first figures since privatisation over the summer, British Energy said market prices in the first half were higher than a year ago but "we do not expect this trend to continue for the remainder of the year."

The company said its alliance on supply with Southern Electric, announced on Thursday, was an example of steps being taken to hedge its price risk in the pool wholesale electricity market and to strengthen its position.
It said improving the financial performance of existing assets "remains a key objective."

British Energy added it would also look at "opportunities to invest profitably in energy projects in the UK and overseas but these will only be pursued where the prospective returns enhance shareholder value."
The company said its share of total electricity demand rose to 21.7 percent from 20.1 percent previously and its achieved selling price rose 0.6 percent to 2.42 pence per kiloWatt hour.
Operating costs per unit of electricity fell 10 percent to 2.18 pence per kiloWatt hour, boosting operating profits to 81 million stg in the first half from 78 million stg previously.

British Energy turned in a loss after tax of 32 million stg on a pro-forma basis for the half year, shrinking 137 million stg from a year ago. It said accrued nuclear liabilities rose by 135 million stg in the first half to 3,868 million stg.
Debt at September 30 totalled 540 million stg with net debt of 360 million stg.
